# Review frontend features and scenes

Organise frontend features around clear ownership and appropriate shared components.

[All skills](index.md) · [Collection overview](../../README.md) · [Research and inspiration](../../standards/framework-evidence.md)

## When to use it

Use when designing or reviewing a frontend against this chosen model.

Example request:

> Review these feature and scene boundaries without changing the framework or underlying frontend rules.

Expected result: A targeted recommendation preserving feature ownership, public surfaces and scene composition.

## A concrete example

This illustrative example starts from the source facts below.

**Source facts and constraints:** Checkout owns its workflow state. The shared button is a UI primitive, and scenes compose features.

**Before**

> The shared button should own the checkout workflow state.

**After**

> Keep checkout workflow state in its feature. Let the scene compose the feature with shared UI primitives.

## Install and use

Install this skill from the versioned collection in a supported Agent Skills environment:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/tree/v1.7.0 --skill frontend-slice-architecture
```

Select the intended agent and installation scope when prompted. This CLI installation is separate from ChatGPT plugin registration and mobile availability. Client discovery and activation require their own verification.

Read the [complete skill instructions](../../skills/frontend-slice-architecture/SKILL.md) and [bundled purpose reference](../../skills/frontend-slice-architecture/references/placement-and-contracts.md) for the full conditions and exceptions.

## Practices behind this skill

The frontend playbook expresses [@pipewrk](https://github.com/pipewrk)'s feature-first architecture rules. Its guidance clarifies ownership and shared-component boundaries without changing the underlying engineering decisions.

- [Microsoft plain-word guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/word-choice/use-simple-words-concise-sentences)
- [Google jargon guidance](https://developers.google.com/style/jargon)

The [source-to-guidance map](../../standards/framework-evidence.md) explains how these sources inform the skill and which decisions are local.
